topic: Visual Design Fundamentals: Layout, Spacing, and Composition
learningObjectives: Apply layout and spacing principles to create organized interfaces.
Identify visual hierarchy using size, position, spacing, contrast, and grouping.
Use alignment and consistent spacing to establish visual relationships.
Improve interface composition by reducing visual clutter and strengthening hierarchy.

activities.title: Visual Hierarchy Explorer
activities.instruction: Select the element users should notice first in the interface.

content.concept: Visual hierarchy controls the order in which users notice and understand interface elements. Size, contrast, position, spacing, and emphasis can make one element more visually dominant than others.
content.tip: Look for the element with the strongest visual emphasis before making your selection.

activities.title: Spacing System Lab
activities.instruction: Adjust the spacing between interface elements until the layout feels organized and easy to scan.

content.concept: Spacing creates relationships between elements. Smaller gaps can show that elements belong together, while larger gaps can separate different sections. A consistent spacing system also prevents interfaces from feeling chaotic.
content.tip: Use smaller spacing within related groups and larger spacing between separate sections.

activities.title: Alignment Builder
activities.instruction: Arrange the interface sections so that their edges and content follow a consistent alignment system.

content.concept: Alignment creates invisible visual lines that connect elements. Consistent alignment makes interfaces easier to scan and gives layouts a stronger sense of order.
content.tip: Look for shared left and right edges between the header, sidebar, and main content.

activities.title: Composition Challenge
activities.instruction: Choose the interface composition that provides the clearest hierarchy with the least visual clutter.

content.concept: Good composition balances hierarchy, alignment, whitespace, grouping, and visual weight. Removing unnecessary decoration and organizing related elements can make an interface easier to understand.
content.tip: Choose the composition where the primary action is clear and related information is grouped logically.

choices: Composition A: Equal-sized elements, inconsistent spacing, and weak grouping
Composition B: Clear hierarchy, consistent spacing, strong alignment, and grouped content
Composition C: Heavy decoration, dense content, and competing visual emphasis
config.answer: Composition B: Clear hierarchy, consistent spacing, strong alignment, and grouped content
